validity.recommendation: existence and classification confirmed; the gem.wiki page's own citations are weak/misattributed, so use the independent sources below instead
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: the gem.wiki page's four citations do NOT actually support this specific pipeline. Two (tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/ and the 'Поточні проекти' page) are generic TSOU corporate pages that 403 on fetch and, per the linked-text/context, never name Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kiev specifically; the LinkedIn cite is a generic company profile with no pipeline-specific content; and the jkg-portal.com.ua article actually describes a 2011 damage incident on the DIFFERENT 'Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv' pipeline (length 454.7 km, diameter 700 mm quoted in the article text) -- i.e. it matches P1452, not P1454, and is misattributed on the wiki page. Per the instructions, a row whose only support is generic/misattributed citations is itself an existence flag -- so I went to independent sources. FOUND, independently: (1) a peer-reviewed-style 2025 academic paper from Dnipro University of Technology (NMU), 'Оцінювання технічного стану переходу магістрального газопроводу «Шебелинка–Диканька–Київ» через залізничну колію' (Vol. 83, issued 2025-12-29), which is an engineering inspection of a railway crossing on this exact named pipeline, explicitly calling it a 'магістральний газопровід' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline, confirming classification) and reporting the crossing 'у працездатному стані' (operational, no critical defects) as of the inspection -- directly supports Status=operating and PipelineType=transmission trunk. (2) Ukrainian Wikipedia's corridor article 'Шебелинка — Київ (газотранспортний коридор)' independently names and describes THREE distinct parallel lines in this corridor: Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv (700 mm, 478 km, 1961) = P1452; Yefremivka-Dikanka-Kyiv (1020 mm, 1970) = P1453; and Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kyiv (1220 mm, 550 km, commissioned 1973) = this row, P1454. Existence is CONFIRMED by two independent, non-GEM sources; classification (trunk transmission gas pipeline) is confirmed by the primary academic source.

validity.recommendation: drop the '2350' component of Diameter -- no source supports a 2350 mm pipe (implausibly large; largest gas trunk pipe worldwide is ~1420 mm); it is very likely a data-entry/transcription error. The remaining ~1200 mm figure is close to (but not identical to) the 1220 mm sourced value -- worth a one-line reconciliation but not itself alarming.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet Diameter = '1200, 2350' mm. No source found anywhere (primary academic paper, Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article, or general search) mentions a 2350 mm diameter for any pipeline in this corridor or in Ukraine generally -- 2350 mm (92.5 in) is far outside the range of any real trunk gas pipeline (the largest in the world run ~1420 mm/56in). The only diameter figure any independent source gives for this specific pipe is 1220 mm (Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article, commissioned 1973), which is close to but not exactly GEM's primary value of 1200 mm -- plausibly a nominal-vs-actual OD rounding difference common in Soviet-era pipe specs, not itself a red flag. The 2350 mm second value has no support and should be removed or investigated as a possible transcription artifact (e.g. digit transposition/duplication).

validity.recommendation: reconcile the 522 km sheet length against the 550 km cited in the Ukrainian corridor source (a ~5% gap) using a primary TSOU technical document (network development plan / GTS map) if it can be accessed -- tsoua.com 403'd for me on every path tried (Cloudflare-blocked), so this is unresolved rather than corrected.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet LengthKnown = 522.00 km. The only independent length figure found, Ukrainian Wikipedia's corridor article, states 550 km for this exact named segment (commissioned 1973). That is a material-ish ~5% disagreement, not a rounding artifact. I could not reach tsoua.com (the GTS operator's own technical pages, which would be the authoritative source) -- every URL on that domain returned HTTP 403 to both the automated verifier and a browser-UA curl fetch, and I could not find an accessible copy via search. Flagging per the spec-disagreement rule rather than silently keeping 522 km or silently substituting 550 km.

validity.recommendation: no merge recommended -- checked against the Dikanka-family cluster (P1452/P1453/P1454/P1460) and found independent confirmation these are distinct parallel Soviet-era trunk lines converging on the Dikanka compressor-station hub, not a double-count; still worth including in any separate cluster-level adjudication pass per the standing instruction not to resolve clusters solo.
validity.researcher_notes: Per the country scope guidance, checked P1454 against the 'Dikanka family' (P1452 Shebelinka-Poltava-Kiev 454.7 km/700mm, P1453 Efremovka-Dikanka-Kiev 477 km/1000mm, P1460 Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Krivyi Rih 272.2 km/700mm). The Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article independently confirms THREE distinct, separately-built parallel lines converging at Dikanka: Shebelinka-Poltava-Kyiv (700mm/478km/1961) = P1452, Yefremivka-Dikanka-Kyiv (1020mm/1970) = P1453, and Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kyiv (1220mm/550km/1973) = P1454 -- a classic Soviet multi-thread trunk buildout, the same pattern as the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II pair (P3484/P5938) noted in the country guidance. P1460 continues on beyond Dikanka toward Kremenchuk/Kryvyi Rih and is a downstream continuation, not an overlapping duplicate of P1454 which terminates at Kyiv. No double-count found for P1454 specifically.

fills.researcher_notes: 2025-12-29 engineering inspection paper (Dnipro University of Technology, Vol. 83) on a railway crossing of this exact pipeline reports the crossing 'у працездатному стані' (operational, no critical defects) as of the inspection date -- direct, recent, independent confirmation the line is in service. Single strong source (the wiki's own citations for this row are generic/misattributed, see validity notes), so tier=medium rather than high; a second independent confirmation of current operating status was not found (tsoua.com blocked every fetch attempt).

Both the NMU engineering paper ('магістральний газопровід' = trunk gas pipeline) and the Wikipedia corridor article (describes the whole corridor as carrying gas from the Shebelinka field) independently confirm this is a natural-gas pipeline.

The pipeline's own name and the corridor article both place its route from the Shebelinka gas field (Kharkiv Oblast) through the Dikanka compressor-station hub (Poltava Oblast) to Kyiv, both endpoints in Ukraine.

This is a general company-level confirmation, not pipeline-specific evidence, hence tier=medium despite two independent sources (tsoua.com's own 'about us'/'key facts' pages, which would be the strongest single source, 403'd on every fetch attempt).

summary: P1454 (Shebelinka-Dikanka-Kiev) is a REAL, correctly-classified operating trunk gas pipeline -- confirmed independently via a 2025 NMU engineering paper and a Ukrainian Wikipedia corridor article, even though the gem.wiki page's own citations are weak/generic or (in one case) misattributed to the different P1452 pipeline. Not a duplicate of P1452/P1453/P1460 (Dikanka family) -- all four are distinct parallel Soviet-era lines. Two spec concerns flagged: the '2350 mm' diameter component has no support anywhere and is very likely a transcription error, and the 522 km sheet length disagrees ~5% with the only independent length figure found (550 km, Wikipedia). Filled Status/Fuel/Location/Owner refs where the existing values checked out.
